ledger.note: 64 BCE: Sampsiceramus I, a Roman client priest-king, kills Antiochus XIII, the last Seleucid but one. 'Sampsiceramus I captured and killed the penultimate Seleucid King Antiochus XIII Asiaticus in 64 BC'; 'a Roman client dynasty of Arab priest-kings known to have ruled by 46 BC from Arethusa' (infobox 'Founded by 46 BC'). The page gives no founding year.
64 BCE: the dynasty is a Roman client. 'Around 64 BC, the Roman General and Triumvir, Pompey had reorganised Syria'; 'a Roman client dynasty of Arab priest-kings'.
48 BCE: the seat moves from Arethusa to Emesa. The page: 'Iamblichus I established it as the new capital' during his reign (48-31 BC) without a year; 48 is the earliest.

30 BCE: Antony's fall ends the kingdom. 'From 30 BC until 20 BC, the Emesene Kingdom was dissolved and became an autonomous community'; Antony had Iamblichus I executed and encouraged his brother Alexander to usurp the throne.
30 BCE: the kingdom becomes an autonomous community under Rome. 'dissolved and became an autonomous community'.
20 BCE: Augustus restores the kingdom. 'Later in 20 BC, Octavian, now as the Roman emperor Augustus, restored the Emesene Kingdom to Iamblichus II.'
20 BCE: Iamblichus II rules as a client priest-king: 'ruled as a Priest-King from 20 BC to 14'.
78: the client kingdom ends. 'after his death in 78, the Kingdom most probably was absorbed by the Roman Province of Syria'; infobox 'Deposition: between 72 and 78/79'.
78: Emesa is absorbed into the province of Syria (the page says 'most probably').

78: the Emesene Kingdom ends. Sohaemus died in 73 and 'was succeeded by his son, Gaius Julius Alexion'; the absorption 'very likely' came between 72 (Vespasian's annexation of Commagene) and the mausoleum's construction.

notes: One page (budget 1-2; Cliopatria has no row for Emesa). The page puts the founding 'by 46 BC' and the first dated event in 64; this dossier starts in 64 (confidence 2). Not on the page: Pompey in 63 (only 'around 64'), the year of Antony's execution of Iamblichus I (reign end 31), Nero's grant of Sophene. Counterpart roman-republic until 30 and roman-empire from 20 (the same convention as kingdom-of-cappadocia). Capital coordinates and the region circles are the usual sites, not from the page. The kingdom was dissolved in 30-20; it is one dossier with a gap (a viewer sees it vanish and return). A gap-filler could open 'Emesa' and 'Sohaemus of Emesa' for the Nero-era lands (Sophene, Arab Iturea).
